lens: Owner and access-sensitive user; cross-step continuity (simulated AI lens)
reason: The public desktop/mobile hero is coherent with Precision Instrument: clear student-consulting proposition, distinct client/student actions and restrained diagram treatment. Source follows the student journey from recruitment preparation to materials and final consent; it accurately distinguishes a profile-free written packet from an original resume that can identify its author. Owner recovery has strong local safeguards: opaque logs, restricted incident identity, preservation after uncertain identity/membership writes, and an explicit resolution receipt that makes no account-repair claim. However, the recovery-to-People handoff loses cycle context. The supplied browser tests exercise a synthetic resolution button, not complete provisioning and recovery with actual provider accounts. These findings and missing integration evidence do not establish world-class task completion; source review is not observed user success.

findings.evidence: The queue accepts an authorized cycleId at lines 34–36 and instructs checking this cycle’s membership at line 66, but Back to People links only to /admin/people. PeoplePage (src/app/admin/people/page.tsx:71–77) accepts no searchParams and independently selects WORKSPACE_ACCESS’s default cycle. src/lib/cycles.ts:36–44 prioritizes status and creation date, so an older-cycle incident can hand off to another cycle. PeopleControls then submits that newly selected cycleId (rush-controls.tsx:68–72).
findings.userImpact: An owner reviewing an older cycle can inspect or grant access in the default cycle instead, then mark the original incident resolved without completing its intended membership repair. Authorization remains enforced, but the authorized target changes across steps.
findings.suggestedFix: Carry cycleId into Back to People and make PeoplePage validate and honor it. Preserve the Access view and incident reference where practical. Add a focused two-cycle recovery journey proving the inspection and repair remain in the incident cycle.

notVerified: No staging or hosted Clerk/Supabase/storage/email integration exists. Actual partial provisioning, session expiry, delayed provider completion and owner repair were not exercised end to end.
The eight passing browser checks use intercepted HTTP and a synthetic harness; the owner queue has source/SSR evidence, without an authenticated visual capture or observed operator completion.

Local SQL evidence covers 709 assertions, including owner-only incident access, revoked-owner denial and idempotent audit resolution. It does not prove deployed migration/application compatibility or provider reconciliation.

No human usability study, assistive-technology session, physical-device, Safari or Firefox verification was supplied. Retention policy and original-resume policy approval remain external decisions; no anonymity or client-outcome endorsement is inferred.
